title: Every-iterate Grothendieck–Lefschetz identity
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum
$p,a,q,k_0,k$, where $q=p^a$. Choose a prime $\ell\neq p$, write
$\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$, choose an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql$, and
choose a finite extension $E/\Ql$ contained in $\Qlb$, and a
separated finite-type
$k_0$-scheme $Y_0$, and
$Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$. Let
$K\in D^b_{c,\mathrm W}(Y,E)$ be a
Weil complex, let
$F$ be its global
geometric-Frobenius action on
compactly supported
cohomology. For every
integer $n\geq1$ and each point $x\in Y_0(\mathbf F_{q^n})$, choose a
geometric point
$\bar x\to Y$ over $x$. The local operators
$F_x^{(n)}$ and the stalk complexes
$K_{\bar x}=L\bar x^*\operatorname{For}(K)$, using the
derived pullback; these are the
local Frobenius and stalk
constructions; their alternating traces are independent of the choices.
The sets $Y_0(\mathbf F_{q^n})$ and their cardinalities $N_n(Y_0)$ use the
point-count convention.
For every such $n$, one has

$$
\sum_{x\in Y_0(\mathbf F_{q^n})}\sum_{j\in\mathbf Z}(-1)^j
\Tr\bigl(F_x^{(n)}\mid
\mathcal H^j(\operatorname{For}K)_{\bar x}\bigr)
=\sum_{i\in\mathbf Z}(-1)^i
\Tr\bigl(F^n\mid H_c^i(Y,K)\bigr).
$$

Both sums are finite. For the constant
Weil sheaf $E_Y$, each local
alternating trace is $1$, so

$$
N_n(Y_0)=\sum_{i\in\mathbf Z}(-1)^i
\Tr\bigl(F^n\mid H_c^i(Y,E)\bigr).
$$

If $Y_0$ is proper,
compactly supported
cohomology may be replaced by
ordinary cohomology. In
particular, let $X_0/\Fq$ be
smooth, proper, geometrically
connected of pure dimension $d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$, put
$X=X_0\times_{\Fq}k$, let $(\Ql)_X$ be its constant
Weil sheaf, and let $F_X$ be the
global geometric Frobenius
on $H^i(X,\Ql)$ for every $i\in\mathbf Z$. Put
$V_{i,\ell}=H^i(X,\Ql)$, $F_{i,\ell}=F_X|_{V_{i,\ell}}$, using the
smooth-proper
cohomological family. Then

$$
N_n(X_0)=\sum_{i=0}^{2d}(-1)^i
\Tr(F_{i,\ell}^n\mid V_{i,\ell}).
$$

proof.text: Fix $n\ge1$ and $P=Y_0(\mathbf F_{q^n})$. By [lem-weil-point-counts-finite], $P$ is finite. By [prop-cohomological-finiteness], $H_c^i(Y,K)$ are finite-dimensional and zero outside a finite interval. By [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace], $H^j(C_{\bar x})$ are finite-dimensional, bounded stalk cohomology. Hence both displayed sums are finite and every trace is defined.

source.place: Proof, trace-identity sentence; agent-formulated extraction of the reviewed seven-step expansion

proof.text: [lem-zl-finite-stage-categorical-trace] gives the categorical equality and comparisons $w_cG_n=\rho(F^n)w_c$, $w_xv_{x,n}=\rho(F_x^{(n)})w_x$ for every chosen geometric point. Apply [lem-zl-condensed-point-supertrace] to these comparisons, using step 1: the two sides become the images of the global alternating trace and the sum of local alternating traces under the same injective ring map $\epsilon_E:E\to\operatorname{End}(U_s)$. This map preserves finite sums and signs. Its zero kernel gives the asserted equality in $E$.

source.place: Proof, trace-identity sentence; agent-formulated extraction of the reviewed seven-step expansion

proof.text: The preceding equality holds for every selection of points by [lem-zl-finite-stage-categorical-trace]. Two selections differing only at $x\in P$ have the same global trace; cancelling the other finite summands proves independence of the local alternating trace at $x$. This compares any two choices. If $P$ is empty the same equality says that the global alternating trace is zero.

source.place: Proof, trace-identity sentence; agent-formulated extraction of the reviewed seven-step expansion

proof.text: For the canonical $E_Y$, [lem-zl-constant-geometric-stalk-unit] identifies every stalk with $E[0]$ and its local operator with the identity. Its trace is $1$ by [def-weil-endomorphism-trace]. Thus the local sum is $\sum_{x\in P}1=\#P=N_n(Y_0)$ by [def-weil-point-counts-zeta], giving the constant-sheaf formula.

source.place: Proof, trace-identity sentence; agent-formulated extraction of the reviewed seven-step expansion

proof.text: For proper $Y_0$, [prop-cohomological-finiteness] supplies $u_i:H_c^i(Y,K)\simeq H^i(Y,K)$ with $u_iF_c=Fu_i$. Induction gives $u_iF_c^n=F^nu_i$. Conjugate matrices have the same trace by [def-weil-endomorphism-trace]; replace each summand, for general $K$ and for $E_Y$.

source.place: Proof, trace-identity sentence; agent-formulated extraction of the reviewed seven-step expansion

proof.text: Take $Y_0=X_0$, $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$. Properness permits step 5. Under the stated smooth-proper pure-dimension-$d$ hypotheses, [prop-cohomological-finiteness] gives $H^i(X,E)=0$ outside $[0,2d]$. The zero-space trace is the empty diagonal sum [def-weil-endomorphism-trace], so discard those terms. Substituting $V_{i,\ell}$ and $F_{i,\ell}$ from [def-weil-smooth-proper-cohomological-family] gives the last formula, also for $d=0$.

proof.text:
The local alternating trace is the one defined in
[def-weil-local-frobenius-trace].
The trace identity and its constant-sheaf and proper-specialization clauses
are supplied by [thm-weil-grothendieck-lefschetz-trace]; finiteness and
the Frobenius action are [prop-cohomological-finiteness]. Thus the
displayed formulae follow.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q82-16c9c14bd (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, both new nodes, every cited statement (from live, since the snapshot dagsnap symlinks are broken; live equals the base for these nodes) and the main-20261015 proof.md, which is a three-sentence pointer to the circular trace theorem. No SGA is used. The item is not in the dropped list and has no live supersession. The re-split note is met: 2 statement-only new nodes of comparable size (about 1.9k and 2.0k characters), and a six-step assembly of about 2.3k characters. Old step 2 (realization, fixed points, right duals, application of nt-assume-trace-formula) became lem-zl-finite-stage-categorical-trace. Old step 5 (constant unit through point transport at finite, integral and rational levels) became lem-zl-constant-geometric-stalk-unit. Old steps 1, 3, 4, 6 and 7 stay as elementary or one-citation steps with the same content; nothing was blurred. Step checks: step 2 applies the supertrace clause to (P_c,G_n,F^n,w_c) and (P_x,v,F_x^(n),w_x), and injectivity of the additive ring map eps_E gives the identity in E. Step 3 is cancellation using the node's every-choice clause; the empty P case is OK. Step 4: E[0] with operator 1 gives trace 1 and #P = N_n. Step 5: the proper comparison H_c^i -> H^i is Frobenius-equivariant and conjugate operators have equal traces. Step 6: vanishing outside [0,2d], and d=0 is covered. The categorical node's hypotheses match the assumption (separated, quasi-compact, locally of finite type, model Frobenius, finite fixed points, right duals). Its every-choice clause is true, but the worker who proves it needs Phi-orbit invariance of stalk traces, because a selection can hit the same fixed point twice; the review notes this. The unit node is true: L xbar^* of the completed integral unit is R lim (A_m)_s, so Fib_s = O_E[0], and a constant section is sent to itself. It generalizes the closed-point E=Q_l clause of lem-zl-constant-sheaf-lseries and is not a duplicate. Batch-5 flags, all accepted: def-weil-local-frobenius-trace (twice) is a definition. lem-zl-general-condensed-weil-realization is an operator comparison with no trace identity, reaching the flagged chapter only through that definition. lem-zl-condensed-point-supertrace reaches only lem-trf-exact-pairing-iso-transport = Mathlib exactPairingCongr. The categorical identity comes only from the leaf nt-assume-trace-formula. Fixes: (1) B2/B3: the unit node's finite-level Weil map is now explicit, theta_m = c_m o lambda_m, with stmt_dep lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback added. (2) The item's split_report tool_uses text said supertrace was used in step 3; corrected to step 2. Accepted tool_uses: lem-weil-point-counts-finite, prop-cohomological-finiteness, lem-zl-condensed-point-supertrace. Advisory: the mathlib_searches verdict strings are copy-pasted across tools.; 2 file(s) fixed by the reviewer
